title: The clear control appears only once you type, and empties the box without closing
preconds:
You need nothing set up beyond being able to sign in. Any records will do.
Sign in to ShopView.
Open the search window: click the Search box in the top bar, or press Ctrl and K together (Cmd and K on a Mac). A panel opens in the middle of the screen with a search box at the top, a row of tabs beneath it (All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices), and either your recent searches or a short line of helper text below that.
Have in mind any word that will find something on your shop - a customer name, part of a work order number, anything. For example on the test shop "Bridgeport" finds a customer; use whatever you know exists on yours.
steps:
With the search window open and nothing typed yet, look at the right-hand end of the search box. Note whether a small clear icon (an x) is showing inside it.
Be careful not to confuse it with "Clear all", which sits to the right of the "Recent searches" heading further down and belongs to your search history, not to the box.
Now type your word into the search box and wait for results.
Look at the right-hand end of the search box again. Note whether the clear icon is showing now.
Click the clear icon.
Note three things: whether the search window is still open, whether the box is now empty, and whether you can carry on typing straight away without clicking back into it.
expected:
Before anything is typed, the clear icon is NOT shown inside the search box. ("Clear all" beside the Recent searches heading is a different control and may be there - it empties your search history, not the box.)
Once something has been typed, the clear icon appears at the right-hand end of the search box.
Clicking it empties the search box.
Clicking it does NOT close the search window - the window stays open, and the cursor stays in the box so you can type again immediately.

Source
Epic SV-9160. The requirement is stated in SV-10068 "UI / UX Fixes" (https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10068), read on 28 September 2026, word for word: "This icon should be only shown when user has typed something in. The other thing is it shouldn't close the search modal, just clear search input" and "Clear icon shouldn't be shown when nothing is typed in."
The Global Search product requirements (Confluence page 576978945) describe the separate "Clear all" action on the Recent searches header, and do not cover the clear control inside the box - which is why this check names SV-10068 as its source.

Last checked against build v26.39.1-02c6b6c on 9/28/2026.

1. Sign in to ShopView with 'Vendor & Order Management' access. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
2. Vendor invoices exist in unpaid, partially paid and paid states.
steps:
1. In the search box, type a term that matches your vendor invoices (so the Unpaid, Partially paid and Paid examples all appear).
2. In the Vendor Invoices group, confirm the group heading and its count appear.
3. Find an Unpaid invoice, a Partially paid invoice and a Paid invoice; for EACH, read its payment status badge and confirm the status text and the design-system colour (confirm all three states render, not just Paid/Unpaid).
4. On a vendor-invoice row, confirm the file-text icon, the invoice number + vendor on the primary line, and the total + invoice date on the second line.
5. Confirm no invoice 'type' is shown on the row, and hover the row to confirm it has no quick action.
expected:
1. Vendor Invoices appear as their own searchable entity, grouped under a 'Vendor Invoices' heading with a count and a scope tab (subject to permission).2. A vendor-invoice row carries the file-text icon; the primary line shows the invoice number + vendor, with the total and the invoice date on the second line.
3. The payment status badge shows the real status using the app's design-system status colours - Paid, Partially paid, or Unpaid (all states, not just Paid/Unpaid).
